fix: filter synthetic confirm_changes tool results in ADK middleware

- Adding some additional tests.

- fix: filter synthetic confirm_changes tool results in ADK middleware

When using predictive state updates, the middleware emits a synthetic
`confirm_changes` tool call to trigger the frontend confirmation dialog.
However, ADK never actually called this tool, so when the frontend sends
back the tool result, ADK throws "No function call event found for
function responses ids" errors.

This fix:
- Filters out `confirm_changes` tool results in `_extract_tool_results`
  before passing them to ADK
- Tracks predictive state tool call IDs to suppress their TOOL_CALL_RESULT
  events (prevents frontend errors about missing function calls)
- Handles the case where all tool results are synthetic (confirm_changes)
  by marking them as processed and continuing with any trailing messages
- Enables follow-up requests after approving/rejecting changes

All 335 tests pass.

  2. Pipes were getting blocked during the `try process.run()` and
    `process.waitUntilExit()` (order of operations were fixed)
  3. We need the binary data for directly piping the `stdout` data to
    `stdin`, and converting the data to a `string`, returns `""` (added a
    new value to the tuple)

I opened a new PR here for this as I did not want to bloat the other PRs
with so many updates. At first I thought of creating a new function
named `runStdinStdout`, but that seemed redundant as it pretty much was
going to do the same thing as `run`.

## Motivation and Context
This PR implements the `container system df` command to display disk
usage statistics for images, containers, and volumes, along with their
total count, active count, size, and reclaimable space for each resource
type.

Active resources are determined by container mount references and
running state, while reclaimable space is calculated from inactive or
stopped resources.

Example output:
```
~/container ❯ container system df
TYPE           TOTAL  ACTIVE  SIZE      RECLAIMABLE
Images         4      3       4.42 GB   516.5 MB (11%)
Containers     4      2       2.69 GB   1.51 GB (56%)
Local Volumes  3      2       208.5 MB  66.2 MB (32%)
```

I'll have some follow-on PRs that will add `-v/--verbose` flag for
detailed per-resource information, `--filter` flag for filtering output
by resource type, and a `--debug` flag for debug statistics like block
usage, clone counts etc.

updates.title: Updates in main (1 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это исправление устраняет ошибку, при которой команда `CLI -it` не могла перенаправлять `stdout`. Ранее внутренний тип `Terminal` ошибочно инициализировался файловым дескриптором `stderr` вместо `stdin`, что мешало корректной работе с `stdout`. Теперь `Terminal` всегда инициализируется с `stdin` (дескриптор 0), а `stdout` и `stderr` получают свои правильные дескрипторы, что обеспечивает корректное перенаправление вывода.
updates.source_content:
- CLI: Fix -it not being able to pipe stdout (#951)

Fixes #949

Typically if one fd is a tty, it's common for all 3 of stdio to be the
same, but that is not always the case. In our case we were using our
Terminal type from Containerization to comb through err/out/in and give
us a type backed by one of the 3 if -t was supplied. It happens that
stderr is the first we check, so our Terminal() is backed by fd 2. This
change modifies things so that we always initialize our Terminal if
asked for with fd 0, and out/err are backed by their corresponding
correct fd number.

updates.title: Updates in main (1 commits)
updates.summary_ru: В команду CLI transcribe добавлена новая функция, позволяющая выводить временные метки на уровне слов. Пользователи могут активировать ее с помощью флага `--word-timestamps`, который отображает точное время и оценки достоверности для каждого слова в расшифровке. Это улучшение упрощает анализ и синхронизацию расшифрованной речи с исходным аудио, обрабатывая и объединяя временные метки на уровне токенов из модели ASR.
updates.source_content:
- Add word-level timestamps support to CLI transcribe command (#193)

## Summary
fixes #189 
This PR adds a new `--word-timestamps` flag that displays timing
information for each word in the transcription output, making it easier
to analyze and synchronize transcribed speech with the original audio.

## Implementation Details

The feature works by:
1. Taking token-level timings from the ASR model output
2. Detecting word boundaries (whitespace characters)
3. Merging consecutive tokens into complete words
4. Averaging confidence scores across tokens that form each word

## Actual CLI Output

```
==================================================
[6:59:58.651 PM] [INFO] [FluidAudio.Transcribe] BATCH TRANSCRIPTION RESULTS
==================================================
[6:59:58.651 PM] [INFO] [FluidAudio.Transcribe] Final transcription:
Hello world!

Word-level timestamps:
  [0] 0.160s - 0.800s: "Hello" (conf: 0.999)
  [1] 0.800s - 1.440s: "world!" (conf: 0.771)

Performance:
  Audio duration: 1.48s
  Processing time: 0.12s
  RTFx: 12.07x
  Confidence: 0.862

[DEBUG] Token timings (count: 5):
  [0] ' H' (id: 425, start: 0.160s, end: 0.480s, conf: 0.998)
  [1] 'ello' (id: 3164, start: 0.480s, end: 0.800s, conf: 1.000)
  [2] ' wor' (id: 2088, start: 0.800s, end: 0.880s, conf: 0.953)
  [3] 'ld' (id: 2493, start: 0.880s, end: 1.360s, conf: 1.000)
  [4] '!' (id: 8020, start: 1.360s, end: 1.440s, conf: 0.362)
```


**Token merging example from output above:**
- ASR tokens: `[" H", "ello", " wor", "ld", "!"]` (5 tokens)
- Merged words: `["Hello", "world!"]` (2 words)
- **"Hello"**: Merged from `" H"` (0.160s-0.480s) + `"ello"`
(0.480s-0.800s) → 0.160s-0.800s
- **"world!"**: Merged from `" wor"` (0.800s-0.880s) + `"ld"`
(0.880s-1.360s) + `"!"` (1.360s-1.440s) → 0.800s-1.440s

---------

updates.title: Updates in main (1 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Этот PR устраняет две проблемы, описанные в Issue #206. Во-первых, класс `EspeakG2P` теперь надёжно находит данные eSpeak NG, даже при вложенных структурах каталогов, благодаря добавлению запасной проверки. Во-вторых, `AppLogger` был улучшен для корректной обработки ошибок ввода-вывода при записи в `stderr`, предотвращая сбои приложения.
updates.source_content:
- Fix Issue #206: eSpeak NG Not Found and Logging Crash (#207)

This PR fixes two issues reported in Issue #206:

1. **eSpeak NG Not Found:** The `EspeakG2P` class now correctly handles
nested `espeak-ng-data` directories (e.g.,
`.../espeak-ng-data/espeak-ng-data/voices`) which can occur in certain
build environments. It also adds a fallback to check the main bundle
resources.
2. **AppLogger Crash:** The `AppLogger` now uses a throwing write method
for `stderr` and handles errors gracefully, preventing crashes when I/O
errors occur.

updates.summary_ru: Это обновление устраняет давнюю проблему на iOS, где данные eSpeak NG не определялись корректно из-за варианта пути `espeak-ng-data.bundle`. Теперь фреймворк корректно проверяет этот вариант `.bundle`, гарантируя нахождение упакованных данных. В результате, неизвестные слова, такие как "FluidAudio", теперь корректно синтезируются на iOS, решая ранее существовавшую проблему.

updates.title: Updates in main (4 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление значительно улучшает управление моделями и системную совместимость. Оно вводит автоматическую группировку сегментированных файлов моделей, решая проблему их отдельного отображения, а также исправляет обнаружение графических процессоров AMD на Windows путем обеспечения правильной настройки переменных окружения. Кроме того, улучшена совместимость с API OpenAI для конечной точки /v1/models и устранены критические ошибки сборки Docker. В релиз также включены незначительные улучшения качества кода и исправления предупреждений.
updates.source_content:
- fix: group sharded model files in auto-discovery (#147) (#157)

* fix: group sharded model files in auto-discovery (#147)

- Add regex-based detection for sharded model patterns (model-XXXXX-of-XXXXX.ext)
- Group multiple sharded files into single model entries with aggregated size
- Display sharded models with count of additional files (e.g., '+3 more files')
- Use directory name as model name for grouped sharded models
- Add comprehensive regression tests for sharded model grouping scenarios
- Clean up unused imports and ensure zero warnings

This resolves the issue where sharded SafeTensors models were listed as
individual entries instead of being grouped together as a single model.

* style: format code with cargo fmt

* fix: remove unused variable prefixes in AMD GPU detection test

- Fixed compilation error where variables were prefixed with underscore but used without underscore
- This was causing test failures during release gate validation

- Fix #142: AMD GPU detection on Windows (#156)

* Fix #142: AMD GPU detection on Windows

- Add configure_gpu_environment() method to set GGML_* environment variables before backend initialization
- Fix GPU layer assignment by ensuring OpenCL/Vulkan/CUDA backends have proper environment setup
- Add comprehensive regression tests for all GPU backend environment configuration
- Fix compiler warnings with documented #[allow(dead_code)] attributes for conditionally-used MoeConfig fields

Root cause: GPU backends require environment variables set before llama.cpp initialization.
AMD GPUs detected by clinfo but layers assigned to CPU due to missing GGML_OPENCL/GGML_VULKAN variables.

Tests: All 6 release gates pass with zero warnings. Regression tests added for GPU backend validation.

* Fix compiler warnings in issue 142 regression test

- Prefix unused variables with underscores to suppress warnings
- Variables are conditionally used based on feature flags

- Fix OpenAI API compatibility for frontend integration (Issue #113) (#155)

- Remove extra fields (root, parent, permission) from /v1/models response
- Create separate ListModel struct for models endpoint that matches OpenAI spec exactly
- Update created timestamp to use proper system time instead of 0
- Update all tests to use the new ListModel structure

Root cause: Frontend applications like Open WebUI and AnythingLLM expect strict OpenAI API compliance. The extra fields in shimmy's Model struct were causing them to reject the API as incompatible.

Fix ensures /v1/models returns only: id, object, created, owned_by - matching OpenAI specification exactly.

- Fix Docker build failure (Issue #152) (#154)

- Add missing COPY benches/ ./benches/ to Dockerfile
- Update Rust version from 1.75-slim to 1.85-slim for lock file compatibility
- Add libclang-dev and cmake build dependencies
- Add Docker build regression test to release gates

Root cause: Dockerfile was missing benches/ directory copy, causing Cargo manifest parsing to fail. Also missing build dependencies for llama.cpp-sys compilation.

updates.title: Updates in main (5 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Этот выпуск в основном сосредоточен на значительных улучшениях и исправлениях в процессе публикации образов Docker. Он вводит автоматическую публикацию как в GHCR, так и в Docker Hub, гарантируя постоянную доступность версионированных тегов и тега "latest", даже если публикация в `crates.io` завершится неудачей. Кроме того, критическое исправление ошибки решает проблему усечения символов Unicode во время потоковой передачи токенов, предотвращая ошибки декодирования UTF-8 путем соблюдения границ многобайтовых символов.
updates.source_content:
- Release workflow: tolerate Cargo.lock changes; always run Docker publish step (avoid skipped GHCR push)

- Use --allow-dirty for crates.io publish to avoid transient Cargo.lock blocking release
- Add git status/diff debug logs for easier triage
- Run Docker publish step even if crates.io publish fails (if: always())

- Release v1.8.1: Fix Docker publishing pipeline

- Added Docker image publishing to GHCR in release workflow
- Fixed issue #146: Docker images now published automatically
- Added proper GHCR authentication and multi-tag publishing
- Both versioned and latest Docker tags now available

- Release v1.8.0: Docker publishing pipeline fix

- Fixed Issue #146: Docker image publishing pipeline failures
- Added automated Docker Hub publishing to release workflow
- Enhanced release gates with Docker build validation
- Improved containerized deployment reliability

- Fix Issue #139: Unicode character handling in token streaming (#159)

- Fixed stop token truncation to respect UTF-8 character boundaries
- Prevents FromUtf8Error when multi-byte characters are split during truncation
- Added regression tests for Unicode handling in token streaming
- Ensures callbacks receive valid UTF-8 strings

The issue was that stop token removal could truncate strings in the middle
of multi-byte Unicode characters (like emojis), causing UTF-8 decoding errors.
Now we find the proper character boundary before the stop token.

- style: format code with cargo fmt (#158)

equivalent and run only once.

updates.title: Updates in main (4 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление значительно улучшает стабильность сборки и выполнения Jank на macOS, особенно в средах nix-darwin. Оно устраняет конфликты между стандартными библиотеками Clang, предоставляемыми ОС и локально собранными, а также улучшает AOT/JIT компиляцию за счет динамической обработки флагов компоновщика и фильтрации путей SDK для обеспечения переносимости. Кроме того, включены улучшения в синтаксический анализ ключевых слов и обработку ошибок.
updates.source_content:
- Clean up and document macOS stdinc fix (#603)

- Add clang args that fix the potential for OS and local Clang build std libs conflicting with each other. (#602)

* Add clang args that fix the potential for OS and local Clang build std libs conflicting with each other.

* Use the new flags conditionally on mac-like platforms.

- Make jank build portable on macOS in nix-darwin environments (#585)

This commit addresses build and runtime issues when jank is compiled on macOS
within a nix-darwin environment, making jank installable via Homebrew on macOS
even when nix-darwin is present.

## Problem

When building in nix-darwin, the SDKROOT and other environment variables are
set to point to nix-managed SDK paths. Although jank builds cleanly on vanilla
macOS, these nix-darwin settings interfere with the build process in two ways:

1. AOT Compilation: Platform-specific linker library requirements need proper
   handling. On macOS, Clang uses libc++ by default and doesn't require explicit
   -lstdc++ linking, while Linux requires it.

2. JIT Compilation: Clang extracts system include paths containing absolute SDK
   paths (e.g., /Applications/Xcode.app/.../MacOSX.sdk/usr/include or
   /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX*.sdk/usr/include). These
   paths get embedded in JANK_JIT_FLAGS and cause header ordering issues at
   runtime when jank performs JIT compilation.

## Solution

### Part 1: Platform-aware AOT compilation with runtime checks
- Moved -lstdc++ linking decision from build-time CMake to runtime C++ code
- Use if constexpr(jtl::current_platform != jtl::platform::macos_like) checks
- This approach is simpler and more maintainable than CMake configuration files
- On macOS: Exclude -lstdc++ (uses libc++ implicitly via Clang)
- On Linux: Include -lstdc++ (requires explicit linking)
- Removed -L/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/lib/unwind which is not needed on macOS

### Part 2: Filter SDK paths from JIT compilation flags
- Create a filtered version of clang_system_include_flags for JIT compilation
- Exclude paths matching /SDKs/ from JIT flags while preserving them for
  the build itself

This separation ensures:
- Build-time includes: Use unfiltered paths (need SDK headers for compilation)
- JIT runtime flags: Use filtered paths (SDK comes from -isysroot at JIT time)

The filtering prevents baking absolute SDK paths into the binary while still
allowing the build itself to find necessary system headers. At JIT time, the
correct SDK is obtained from -isysroot dynamically rather than hardcoded
build-time paths, making jank portable across different macOS/Nix configurations.

## Verification
- Builds successfully with SDKROOT set (nix-darwin environment)
- Builds successfully on vanilla macOS
- JIT compilation works correctly with filtered flags
- All check-health tests pass
- AOT compilation generates correct platform-specific binaries

- [TransferEngine] Support DP in transfer engine

Now the transfer engine supports both DP and TP.
This is needed for *D*P *D*eepseek with *D*I (The Triple-*D*).

The main difference now is that we specify the src and dst replica
indices
when we begin a transfer. Notice that the src and dst replicas can
differ.
```
// before
transfer_engine.initiate_send_transfer(
    remote_metadata=remote_metadata,
    src_idxs=src_idxs,
    dst_idxs=dst_idxs,
)

// after
transfer_engine.initiate_send_transfer(
    remote_metadata=remote_metadata,
    src_idxs=src_idxs,
    dst_idxs=dst_idxs,
    src_replica_idx=src_replica_idx,
    dst_replica_idx=dst_replica_idx,
)
```

Like how we already support TP, we use different NixlAgent per gpu for
DP.

There is no change needed at the NIXL layer. All the changes are purely
at
the Python transfer engine layer to support `list[list[Tensor]]` instead
of just `list[Tensor]`.

Although transfer engine supports DP + TP at same time, the rest of the
stack does not support them in combination yet fyi.

In a followup PR I will test that DP Llama works.

updates.summary_ru: Это обновление упрощает настройку распределенного вывода (DI), унифицируя переменные окружения и требуя явного указания целевых конечных точек для запросов. Основные улучшения производительности включают значительно ускоренные ядра редукции GPU (до 3 раз), увеличение пропускной способности на 13% для рабочих нагрузок Qwen за счет оптимизации планировщика, а также начальную поддержку операторов сравнения SIMD в предложениях `where`. Релиз также исправляет критические ошибки, такие как состояния гонки в тестах с использованием нескольких GPU и проблемы с разделяемой памятью ZMQ при межузловой связи, а также добавляет функции квантования NVFP4.

- [DI] Simplify DI env vars and delete default destination address.

The env vars needed to configure DI are way too convoluted. I am
simplifying them here.

Sample old env var:
```
MAX_SERVE_DISPATCHER_CONFIG='{"transport": "dynamic_zmq", "transport_config": {"bind_address": "tcp://10.0.0.207:7000", "default_destination_address": "tcp://10.0.0.229:6000"}}'
```

This is annoying since it is a json string and we need to take care due
to double quotes and spaces.
You can easily mispecify this due to string escaping woes.

Additionally, it allows us to configure the transport type
("dynamic_zmq") when there are no other options.

Finally, it allows us to pass the "default_destination_address". This
refers to the default prefill node
to forward a request by a decode node if the target endpoint is not
specified for the request. This field
is meaningless for prefill nodes since they do not forward requests. I
am deleting this field and making it
a hard error if target endpoint is not specified for a request.

Now the new env var is much simpler:
```
MAX_SERVE_DI_BIND_ADDRESS=tcp://10.0.0.207:7000
```

This is a simple string that is easy to specify and read.

---

I am on privileged Gcore 2x8xH100 with Infiniband. This is two nodes
with 8 GPUs each.

Here is how to run deepseek with DI. We do not use multi-node EP here.

We use the `kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random` version since full
deepseek
does not fit on one 8xh100 node.

MODULAR_DEVICE_CONTEXT_BUFFER_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT=95 is specified to
leave room
for nvshmem which allocates memory via cuMemCreate. If I set 99, I get a
crash
during inititalization.

prefill-chunk-size=128 is specified to minimize the amount of memory
that
nvshmem allocates.

---

Before:
```
// launch on decode node
MODULAR_DEVICE_CONTEXT_BUFFER_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT=95 \
  MAX_SERVE_SCHEDULER_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_S=0 \
  UCX_TLS="rc,ud,dc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc" \
  UCX_NET_DEVICES="mlx5_ib0:1,mlx5_ib1:1,mlx5_ib2:1,mlx5_ib3:1,mlx5_ib4:1,mlx5_ib5:1,mlx5_ib6:1,mlx5_ib7:1" \
  MAX_SERVE_DISPATCHER_CONFIG='{"transport": "dynamic_zmq", "transport_config": {"bind_address": "tcp://10.0.0.207:7000", "default_destination_address": "tcp://10.0.0.229:6000"}}' \
  br //max -- serve --model-path=kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random \
  --pipeline-role=decode_only --devices=gpu:0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 --ep-size=8 --prefill-chunk-size=128

// launch on prefill node
MODULAR_DEVICE_CONTEXT_BUFFER_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT=95 \
  MAX_SERVE_SCHEDULER_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_S=0 \
  UCX_TLS="rc,ud,dc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc" \
  UCX_NET_DEVICES="mlx5_ib0:1,mlx5_ib1:1,mlx5_ib2:1,mlx5_ib3:1,mlx5_ib4:1,mlx5_ib5:1,mlx5_ib6:1,mlx5_ib7:1" \
  MAX_SERVE_DISPATCHER_CONFIG='{"transport": "dynamic_zmq", "transport_config": {"bind_address": "tcp://10.0.0.229:6000", "default_destination_address": "deadbeef"}}' \
  br //max -- serve --model-path=kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random \
  --pipeline-role=prefill_only --devices=gpu:0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 --ep-size=8 --prefill-chunk-size=128 --headless

// send request to decode node. leave target endpoint unspecified so we use the default destination address.
curl -N http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random",
    "max_tokens": 50,
    "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Who won the World Series in 2020?"}
    ]
}'
```

After:
```

  MAX_SERVE_DI_BIND_ADDRESS=tcp://10.0.0.207:7000 \
  br //max -- serve --model-path=kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random \
  --pipeline-role=decode_only --devices=gpu:0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 --ep-size=8 --prefill-chunk-size=128

// launch on prefill node

  MAX_SERVE_SCHEDULER_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_S=0 \
  UCX_TLS="rc,ud,dc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc" \

  MAX_SERVE_DI_BIND_ADDRESS=tcp://10.0.0.229:6000 \
  br //max -- serve --model-path=kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random \
  --pipeline-role=prefill_only --devices=gpu:0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 --ep-size=8 --prefill-chunk-size=128 --headless

// send request to decode node while specifying the target endpoint
curl -N http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "kathywu95/deepseek-v3-small-random",
    "max_tokens": 50,
    "target_endpoint": "tcp://10.0.0.229:6000",
    "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},

finished memsetting its signals buffer, or vice versa.

bt-h100 //max/tests/integration/API/python:multi_gpu_tests/test_allgather --runs_per_test=100
```

changes in this PR, I no longer see any timeouts.

- [MAX] Don't divide batch size by Data Parallelism degree

When you specify --data-parallel-degree 8 --max-batch-size 32 there are
two ways to interpret this:
1. Each of the 8 DP replicas has a cap on batch size of 32. Across all
replicas the aggregate max batch size is thus 8 * 32 = 256.
2. Each of the 8 DP replicas has a cap on batch size of 4. Across all
replicas the aggregate max batch size is thus 32.

Currently our code uses interpretation #2. However, I think we should
switch to #1 for the following reasons:
- Maintaining max_batch_size and max_batch_size_per_replica is very
error prone. It is very easy to mix them up.
- This interpretation is consistent to what vLLM does.

- [mojo-lang] Struct extensions naming/importing changes, attempt 2 (#72954)

Re-merges the compiler parts of
[Internal link] which were always fine
but caught up in the revert of the stdlib changes.

This PR does three main changes:

* Cleanup: Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) known to their
parents not as their struct's name ("MyStruct") but instead prefixed
with "extension:" ("extension:MyStruct"). This makes it so
lookupAndResolveDecl("MyStruct") doesn't return the extensions as well.
This is good because we generally like finding and resolving as little
as possible.
* Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) also known to their parents
as "extension:". This is helpful when we want to look up "all extensions
in a given scope", which is useful for the next point.
* Makes it so when we import anything from a module, we also import all
extensions (we just look for anything named "extension:").

Note that this might not be the final design, this makes an assumption
that if a file wants to use an extension, then that extension is in a
file that is indirectly imported. It's similar to Rust/Swift/C#/Kotlin,
but we might want to be more similar to Python, which just makes all
extensions globally visible to everyone everywhere, despite all the
spooky action at a distance that entails (doc incoming on this).

### [Kernels][FP4] Add NVFP4 dynamic scaled quantization kernel

This PR adds a quantization kernel for FP4 Activations. It follows the
same implementation as flashInfer and vLLM. For correctness check,
simillar to flashInfer we
use `rtol=atol=1e-1` for scalers and `rtol=1e0, atol=1e-1` for output
values. This is due to limitted accuracy of FP4 value. For example,
Float32(2.5) is mapped to FP4(2.0) and Float32(2.500001) is mapped to
3.0. Another approach for correctness check is to count number of errors
  and make sure they are less than a threshold.

Current limitations:

1. Only supports with NVFP4 (with minor changes it can also support
   MXFP4/MXFP8)
2. Only supports 2D (MxN) tensors for which `N % 8 == 0`.
3. Performance-wise it's not the ideal implementation and it can

- [mojo-lang] Struct extensions naming/importing changes (#72612)

Re-merges the compiler parts of
[Internal link] which were always fine
but caught up in the revert of the stdlib changes.

This PR does three main changes:

* Cleanup: Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) known to their
parents not as their struct's name ("MyStruct") but instead prefixed
with "extension:" ("extension:MyStruct"). This makes it so
lookupAndResolveDecl("MyStruct") doesn't return the extensions as well.
This is good because we generally like finding and resolving as little
as possible.
* Makes extensions (eg extension MyStruct) also known to their parents
as "extension:". This is helpful when we want to look up "all extensions
in a given scope", which is useful for the next point.
* Makes it so when we import anything from a module, we also import all
extensions (we just look for anything named "extension:").

Note that this might not be the final design, this makes an assumption
that if a file wants to use an extension, then that extension is in a
file that is indirectly imported. It's similar to Rust/Swift/C#/Kotlin,
but we might want to be more similar to Python, which just makes all
extensions globally visible to everyone everywhere, despite all the
spooky action at a distance that entails (doc incoming on this).

- [stdlib] Simplify SIMD dunder relational methods

This commit simplifies several SIMD dunder relational methods.

The methods work by calling into their respective non-dunder variants,
which return SIMD bool vectors. Those are then used to create a `Bool`
using the constructor and the `ImplicitlyBoolable` trait, which calls
back into SIMD's `__bool__` method.

Instead, we can avoid this roundtrip by calling `__bool__` ourselves.
This keeps things in the SIMD domain and avoids the trait interface.

An added benefit of this is that this specific `Bool` constructor is not
supported by `@always_inline("builtin")` due to an unsupported argument
convention. Future work will thus be able to mark these dunder
relational methods `@always_inline("builtin")` and enable better support
for SIMD types in `where` clauses.

updates.summary_ru: Это обновление значительно развивает язык Mojo, стандартную библиотеку и производительность ядра. В нем представлены улучшения вывода типов параметров с введением типа `Never`, удалены параметры `result` и реализован нативный ввод-вывод файлов, а также усовершенствования стандартной библиотеки, включая SIMD-оптимизации и новые утилиты `os`. Повышение производительности достигается за счет новых слоев внимания, ядер FP8/FP4, обширных миграций ядер (например, с `HostNDBuffer`) и улучшений бенчмаркинга, что дополняется повышением стабильности тестов на macOS и крупными обновлениями файла README для улучшения взаимодействия с сообществом.

This teaches Mojo to infer generic error types to `Never` when presented with a function that doesn't raise. This completes the core support for "parametric raises" by subsuming the Swift "rethrows" extension. For example, given a generic map function: ```mojo # This simple "map" function is generic over closure throwability. fn int_list_map[ ErrorType: AnyType ]( mut list: List[Int], fp: fn (arg: Int) raises ErrorType -> Int ) raises ErrorType: for ref elt in list: elt = fp(elt) # Example function that raises. fn partial_function(arg: Int) raises -> Int: if arg > 100: raise Error("Argument too large") return arg * 2 # Example function that does not raise. fn complete_function(arg: Int) -> Int: return arg + 1 # Usage examples fn examples(mut list: List[Int]): # This can throw so it needs to be in a try block. try: int_list_map(list, partial_function) except err: print(err) # This can't throw so it doesn't need to be in a try block. int_list_map(list, complete_function) ``` MODULAR_ORIG_COMMIT_REV_ID: 2adf059f3f7ab3be41c439bf46c537fe5d1b50cd - [stdlib] polish: Remove ambiguous `String.join` variadic overload (Part 2.5/N) This avoids a change in overload resolution behavior that will occur when making `List` conform to `Writable`. Code such as `"foo".join([1, 2, 3])` ought to resolve to the `String.join(Span)` overload, but could theoretically also resolve to this removed variadic overload as a single-element variadic argument pack. That does not occur today because the variadic overload requires the elements to implement `Writable`, which `List` does not _today_. To avoid a bug in a subsequent PR that _does_ add a `List(Writable)` conformance, simply remove this overload. This is directionally right longer term, as Python does not have a variadic `str.join()` method, only a method that takes an `Iterable`. updates.summary_ru: Это обновление включает обширный рефакторинг в ядре (kernels) и стандартной библиотеке, в частности, перенос многочисленных тестов ядра и кода матричного умножения для ЦП с `HostNDBuffer` на другие механизмы. - [stdlib] polish: Use `T: ConvertibleToPython` in args instead of `PythonObject` (Part 2/N)

As part of aiming at removing the `@implicit` decorator from
`PythonObject` initializers, but to preserve the ability to do things like:

    var obj = PythonObject(5)

    var res = obj * 5

it is necessary that e.g. `PythonObject.__mul__` change from taking the
RHS as a `PythonObject`, and instead take a `T: ConvertibleToPython`.

From a callers perspective, this is largely the same: you can pass
simple values like `5` and it gets converted to a `PythonObject` either way.

But making the conversion be part of `__mul__` instead of a general
feature of `PythonObject` means that such implicit conversions can be avoided in
cases where they would be surprising.

NOTE: This has some known caveats / issues of it's own, but we believe
those are less-bad than leaving the current `@implicit` decorators as they are.

Known issues include:

* This technically will enable _more_ types to be "implicitly" converted
to PythonObject
* This makes these functions generic, potentially increasing code size
and compile times.
(These functions like likely commonly be stamped out with multiple
different input parameter types)

- [stdlib] Migrate a few `is_unsigned` checks to where clauses

Migrate a few uses of `__comptime_assert dtype.is_unsigned()` to use

MODULAR_ORIG_COMMIT_REV_ID: e2d93cc543ee16fdaffddc79950c157aafdefdcd

- [stdlib] Migrate a few `is_integral` checks to where clauses

This commit migrates some uses of `__comptime_assert
dtype.is_integral()` to `where dtype.is_integral()` clauses on function
signatures. This provides better type safety by enabling compile-time
constraint checking.

The remaining 22 `is_integral` uses cannot be migrated due to a compiler
limitation: the constraint propagation system cannot prove constraints
when:

1. **Call sites lack constraint evidence**: Functions are called from
contexts where the compiler cannot prove the dtype is integral (e.g.,
from `builtin/simd.mojo`, `io/write.mojo`)

2. **Calling non-always-inline-builtin functions**: Functions use DTypes
returned from compile-time functions like `get_accum_type[dtype]()`, and
the compiler cannot evaluate non-builtin functions to infer their return
type properties

3. **Transitive constraint dependencies**: Functions call other
functions that require constraints, creating chains where evidence
cannot propagate through multiple levels

We explored using `@always_inline("builtin")` as a workaround for
constraint propagation, but this annotation is too restrictive:

- Does not support `@parameter if` statements
- Does not support `__comptime_assert`
- Does not support some `llvm_intrinsic` patterns
- Even with `where` clauses, call sites still cannot prove constraints

- [LoRA] Fix a bug with the sequence boundary between the K and V
extension of the input-row-offsets

Fix a bug introduced with the LoRA KV optimizations. Instead of using
the end of the LoRA sequences for the KV offsets boundary, I foolishly
used the end of the whole sequence as the boundary. For example, lets
say we have 4 requests and 2 use LoRA. If our `total_seq_len = 256` and
our `lora_seq_len = 128`, then prior to this fix, we would create a
tensor of size `total_seq_len * 2` and our `lora_grouped_offsets = [0,
64, 128, 320, 384]`. Our first group in V would span 192 tokens which is
completely incorrect. The KV computation needs to know where the LoRA
sequences end and also needs a properly sized tensor to support this
computation correctly. The correct tensor of size is `lora_seq_len * 2`
and our offsets should be `lora_grouped_offsets=[0,64,128 192, 256]`.
Now group 0 in V is correctly 64 tokens instead of 128.

- [stdlib] Fix file permissions on ARM64 macOS

The `open()` syscall is a C variadic function, and `external_call`
doesn't correctly pass the mode argument on ARM64 macOS due to calling
convention differences. This caused files to be created with incorrect
permissions (0310 instead of 0666), resulting in "Permission denied"
errors.

This fix adds an `fchmod()` call after `open()` to correct file
permissions when creating new files. Also re-enables tests that were
disabled on macOS and updates test files to use `gettempdir()`
consistently.

(#11536) ### What problem does this PR solve? ##### Problem Description When parsing HTML files, some page content may be lost. For example, text inside nested `` tags within multiple `
` elements (e.g., `
Text_1
Text_2
`) fails to be preserved correctly. ###### Root Cause #1: Block ID propagation is interrupted 1. **Block ID generation**: When the parser encounters a `
`, it generates a new `block_id` because `
` belongs to `BLOCK_TAGS`. 2. **Recursive processing**: This `block_id` is passed down recursively to process the `
`’s child nodes. 3. **Interruption occurs**: When processing a child `` tag, the code enters the `else` branch of `read_text_recursively` (since `` is a Tag). 4. **Bug location**: The first line in this `else` branch explicitly sets **`block_id = None`**. - This discards the valid `block_id` inherited from the parent `
`. - Since `` is not in `BLOCK_TAGS`, it does not generate a new `block_id`, so it passes `None` to its child text nodes. 5. **Consequence**: The extracted text nodes have an empty `block_id` in their `metadata`. During the subsequent `merge_block_text` step, these texts cannot be correctly associated with their original `
` block due to the missing ID. As a result, all text from `` tags gets merged together, which then triggers a second issue during concatenation. 6. **Solution:** Remove the forced reset of `block_id` to `None`. When the current tag (e.g., ``) is not a block-level element, it should inherit the `block_id` passed down from its parent. This ensures consistent ownership across the hierarchy: `div` → `font` → `text`. ###### Root Cause #2: Data loss during text concatenation 1. The line `current_content += (" " if current_content else "" + content)` has a misplaced parenthesis. When `current_content` is non-empty (`True`): - The ternary expression evaluates to `" "` (a single space). - The code executes `current_content += " "`. - **Result**: Only a space is appended—**the new `content` string is completely discarded**. ### Type of change - [x] Bug Fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- fix: resolve "'bool' object has no attribute 'items'" in SDK enabled … (#11725)

### What problem does this PR solve?
Fixes the `AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'items'` error
when updating the `enabled` parameter of a document via the Python SDK
(Issue #11721).

Background: When calling `Document.update({"enabled": True/False})`
through the SDK, the server-side API returned a boolean `data=True` in
the response (instead of a dictionary). The SDK's `_update_from_dict`
method (in `base.py`) expects a dictionary to iterate over with
`.items()`, leading to an immediate AttributeError during response
parsing. This prevented successful synchronization of the updated
`enabled` status to the local SDK object, even if the server-side
database/update index operations succeeded.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug Fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
### Additional Context (optional, for clarity)
- **Root Cause**: Server returned `data=True` (boolean) for `enabled`
parameter updates, violating the SDK's expectation of a dictionary-type
`data` field.
- **Fix Logic**: 
1. Removed the separate `return get_result(data=True)` in the `enabled`
update branch to unify response flow.
  2. 
- **Backward Compatibility**: No breaking changes—other update scenarios
(e.g., renaming documents, modifying chunk methods) remain unaffected,
and the response format stays consistent.

- feat(gcs): Add support for Google Cloud Storage (GCS) integration (#11718)

### What problem does this PR solve?

This Pull Request introduces native support for Google Cloud Storage
(GCS) as an optional object storage backend.

Currently, RAGFlow relies on a limited set of storage options. This
feature addresses the need for seamless integration with GCP
environments, allowing users to leverage a fully managed, highly
durable, and scalable storage service (GCS) instead of needing to deploy
and maintain third-party object storage solutions. This simplifies
deployment, especially for users running on GCP infrastructure like GKE
or Cloud Run.

The implementation uses a single GCS bucket defined via configuration,
mapping RAGFlow's internal logical storage units (or "buckets") to
folder prefixes within that GCS container to maintain data separation.
This architectural choice avoids the operational complexities associated
with dynamically creating and managing unique GCS buckets for every
logical unit.

- fix: set default embedding model for TEI profile in Docker deployment (#11824)

## What's changed
fix: unify embedding model fallback logic for both TEI and non-TEI
Docker deployments

> This fix targets **Docker / `docker-compose` deployments**, ensuring a
valid default embedding model is always set—regardless of the compose
profile used.

##  Changes

| Scenario | New Behavior |
|--------|--------------|
| **Non-`tei-` profile** (e.g., default deployment) | `EMBEDDING_MDL` is
now correctly initialized from `EMBEDDING_CFG` (derived from
`user_default_llm`), ensuring custom defaults like `bge-m3@Ollama` are
properly applied to new tenants. |
| **`tei-` profile** (`COMPOSE_PROFILES` contains `tei-`) | Still
respects the `TEI_MODEL` environment variable. If unset, falls back to
`EMBEDDING_CFG`. Only when both are empty does it use the built-in
default (`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`), preventing an empty embedding model.
|

##  Why This Change?

- **In non-TEI mode**: The previous logic would reset `EMBEDDING_MDL` to
an empty string, causing pre-configured defaults (e.g., `bge-m3@Ollama`
in the Docker image) to be ignored—leading to tenant initialization
failures or silent misconfigurations.
- **In TEI mode**: Users need the ability to override the model via
`TEI_MODEL`, but without a safe fallback, missing configuration could
break the system. The new logic adopts a **“config-first,
env-var-override”** strategy for robustness in containerized
environments.

##  Implementation

- Updated the assignment logic for `EMBEDDING_MDL` in
`rag/common/settings.py` to follow a unified fallback chain:

EMBEDDING_CFG → TEI_MODEL (if tei- profile active) → built-in default


##  Testing

Verified in Docker deployments:

1. **`COMPOSE_PROFILES=`** (no TEI)  
 → New tenants get `bge-m3@Ollama` as the default embedding model 
2. **`COMPOSE_PROFILES=tei-gpu` with no `TEI_MODEL` set**  
 → Falls back to `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`   
3. **`COMPOSE_PROFILES=tei-gpu` with `TEI_MODEL=my-model`**  
 → New tenants use `my-model` as the embedding model

updates.title: Updates in main (66 commits)
updates.summary_ru:
The recent updates significantly refactor the application's authentication system by entirely removing WorkOS integration and implementing auto-login for single-user mode. Furthermore, environment variables for both backend and frontend have been consolidated into a single source, simplifying configuration. New features include adding team and workspace management with migration capabilities, alongside various bug fixes and improvements to diffusion paths and seeding processes.

Недавние обновления значительно переработали систему аутентификации приложения, полностью удалив интеграцию с WorkOS и внедрив автоматический вход для однопользовательского режима. Кроме того, переменные окружения для бэкенда и фронтенда были объединены в единый источник, что упрощает конфигурацию. Новые функции включают добавление управления командами и рабочими пространствами с поддержкой миграции, а также различные исправления ошибок и улучшения путей распространения и процессов инициализации.

updates.summary_ru: Данное обновление интегрирует API Google Gemini 3 в конвейер оптического распознавания символов (OCR). Оно также включает значительный рефакторинг удаленного APIClient, направленный на улучшение читаемости кода, стандартизацию обработки ошибок (с генерированием только исключений, производных от TensorlakeError), обеспечение единообразной политики повторных попыток и предоставление более понятных сообщений об ошибках. Помимо этого, были рефакторингированы тесты контекста запросов, фронтенд теперь обрабатывает операции чтения/записи больших двоичных объектов (BLOB), а также исправлена ошибка в его логгере.
updates.source_content:
- feat: google gemini in ocr pipeline provider (#454)

## Descriptioin

- The addition of Google Gemini 3 API in OCR Models.

- Refactor and fix remote APIClient (#451)

The current remote APIClient code was derived from a fairly old SDK code
base. Because of this remote APIClient has both stylistic issues and
coding bugs now.

This PR does the following:

* Add type hints everywhere to make it easier to read code.
* Don't user variadic args and kwargs as it makes reading code harder.
* Only raise exceptions derived from TensorlakeError. We were raising
arbitrary unexpected exception types directly into user code while all
SDK code should raise exceptions derived from TensorlakeError.
* Use consistent retry policy in sse stream and regular http requests.
* Remove unused pydantic model definitions for Server API. We'll add the
models back if we need them in future projects. Having them in remote
APIClient requires us keeping them updated which might slow down some
future work. This is also effectively a dead code.
* Define code structure in remote APIClient that other people can follow
in the future and not introduce hard to notice mistakes because it's
Python.
* Give more descriptive user friendly error messages in certain cases
like no auth credentials present on HTTP 401 code.
* Don't use httpx client event hooks because they make the APIClient
error handling behavior hard to reason about i.e. it makes exceptions
raised by ApiClient dependant on how it was created. The existing hooks
raise ClickException which has nothing to do with TensorlakeError which
is a base class for all errors in SDK components which include
APIClient.

Testing:

* Checked all callers of APIClient methods to make sure that none of
them break if we start only raising TensorlakeError derived exceptions.
* Manually ran all tensorlake CLI commands.
* All integration tests pass.

- Refactor request context tests (#453)

Move them to a dedicated directory and add missing basic tests for
existing API.

- Move request state read/writes into FE (#448)

The BLOBs (presigned URLs) for reading/writing are supplied by Executor.
Actual read/writes are done on FE side.

Also fix FE logger bug introduced after we started to use Cloud Events
to print FE logs. The FE logger started to fail logging if a log tag is
not json serializable. FE logger must be absolutely reliable and not
raise exceptions itself.

All tests pass locally with Indexify PR
https://github.com/tensorlakeai/indexify/pull/1892

updates.summary_ru: Этот апдейт повышает надежность отчетов о прогрессе и генерации CloudEvent путем стандартизации JSON-сериализации. Введена `SerializationError` для явной обработки сбоев при сериализации значений, что применимо к `FunctionProgress.update` и CloudEvents. Кроме того, обновления прогресса теперь включают имена функций и атрибуты, временные метки соответствуют ISO 8601, а комплексные тесты обеспечивают корректную сериализацию и обработку ошибок.
updates.source_content:
- Fix progress update serialization. (#456)

Document and raise SerializationError if we cannot serialize a value to
JSON.
Include tests for cloud events and progress updates.

Fixes #450 


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Ensure progress and cloud events are JSON-serializable, include
function name and message in progress updates, and add comprehensive
tests.
> 
> - **Progress reporting**:
> - `FunctionProgress.update` now accepts `attributes: dict[str, str] |
None` and documents `SerializationError` on JSON failures.
> - Local progress (`LocalFunctionProgress`) prints default "executing
step X of Y" and formats optional `message` + JSON `attributes`; raises
`SerializationError` on serialization failure.
> - FE progress proxy (`ProxiedAllocationProgress`) enriches events with
`function_name`, default message, and forwards `attributes`.
> - **CloudEvents**:
> - `print_cloud_event`/`new_cloud_event` accept optional `message`
(added to top-level event) and use `_serialize_json` that raises
`SerializationError` on failure.
> - Timestamp generation refactored (`_current_time`) to ISO 8601 with
timezone offset; internal helpers renamed.
> - **Tests**:
> - Add unit tests for CloudEvent structure, timestamps, serialization,
and stdout printing (including custom `type`/`source`/`message`).
> - Add tests for local and FE progress updates (with/without custom
messages) validating event payloads and attributes.
> - Add negative tests asserting `SerializationError` surfacing on
non-serializable data (captured in stderr/exception).
> - **Version**:
>   - Bump `pyproject.toml` version to `0.2.86`.

updates.summary_ru: Функции Tensorlake теперь имитируют обычные функции Python, копируя метаданные, что значительно улучшает их совместимость с агентскими фреймворками, такими как OpenAI, и позволяет корректно генерировать описания инструментов. Пример `city_guide` был значительно переработан, чтобы продемонстрировать контейнеризованные инструменты с подробными докстрингами и включить вспомогательную функцию для безопасного удаленного выполнения кода для таких задач, как конвертация температуры.
updates.source_content:
- Add message update to documentai sdk (#458)

- Tensorlake Function mimic regular functions and extend city guide readme example (#460)

Make Tensorlake Functions mimic regular functions as much as possible
    
This results in correctly generated tool descriptions by OpenAI agentic
framework, i.e. after updating the city guide example in this PR the
weather tool description in the created agent is exactly the same as
when no @function() decorator is used:
    
    ```
Agent(name='Guide Creator', handoff_description=None,
tools=[FunctionTool(name='weather_tool', description='',
params_json_schema={'properties': {'city': {'title': 'City', 'type':
'string'}}, 'required': ['city'], 'title': 'weather_tool_args', 'type':
'object', 'additionalProperties': False}, on_invoke_tool=<function
function_tool.<locals>._create_function_tool.<locals>._on_invoke_tool at
0x10ca5d5a0>, strict_json_schema=True, is_enabled=True,
tool_input_guardrails=None, tool_output_guardrails=None),
    ```

Now OpenAI `@function_tool` decorator can be applied to a Tensorlake
Function. The OpenAI decorator has to be at the top of the decorator
chain because it returns a non-callable dataclass. This approach would
work for other agentic frameworks without any extra custom
wrappers/decorators needed per agentic framework. I did an
implementation that requires minimal changes where our Function object
mimics as much as possible to a regular python function. If we find that
this mimicking is not sufficient for some other agentic frameworks then
we can do a full more intrusive implementation where we generate regular
python functions. This would 100% work in all cases with all frameworks
but requires more work and maintenance complexity so I'm doing doing
this now because the already implemented approach might work for all the
frameworks too.

Extending city guide example:

Add remote code execution in a function container to convert
temperature. Trigger temperature conversion by running the agent for
Milan, Italy. Format long strings nicer. Add docstrings to all tools so
Agent can potentially use them better. This also shows a more canonical
agent code to users. Also verified that it works in remote mode on
Tensorlake Cloud.

Output:

```
Generating city guide for: Milan, Italy

Getting weather for: Milan, Italy
Finding activity for Milan, Italy with weather: Mostly cloudy, 48°F (9°C)
Creating guide for Milan, Italy

==================================================
CITY GUIDE
==================================================

Milan, Italy

Weather: Mostly cloudy, 9 °C.
Guide: It’s a cool, cloudy day—perfect for visiting the Civic Aquarium of Milan. Enjoy exploring over 100 aquatic species inside a beautiful Art Nouveau building near Sempione Park, making this a relaxing indoor escape!
```



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Copy original function metadata to improve agent tool introspection
and revamp the city_guide example with containerized tools and a safe
code-exec helper for Celsius conversion.
> 
> - **SDK/Core**:
> - Function now mimics user functions by copying metadata (e.g.,
`__doc__`, `__name__`, `__qualname__`, `__code__`, annotations),
improving agent/tool introspection.
> - **Example: `examples/readme_example/city_guide.py`**:
> - Introduce `FUNCTION_CONTAINER_IMAGE` and apply it to all
tools/application.
> - Convert tools to `*_tool` functions with `@function_tool` +
`@function` and richer docstrings/instructions.
> - Add `run_unsafe_python_code` to execute untrusted Python in an
isolated container (timeout, tempfile + subprocess).
> - Update `create_guide_tool` to use `convert_to_celsius_tool` that
delegates conversion via the safe code-exec function.
> - Default city set to `"Milan, Italy"` and minor formatting
improvements.
> - **Misc**:
>   - Fix comment typo in `introspect.py`.
>   - Bump version to `0.2.87` in `pyproject.toml`.
>

updates.source_content:
- feat(tools): Add debug logging to VertexAiSearchTool

Merge https://github.com/google/adk-python/pull/3284

**Problem:**
When debugging agents that utilize the `VertexAiSearchTool`, it's currently difficult to inspect the specific configuration parameters (datastore ID, engine ID, filter, max_results, etc.) being passed to the underlying Vertex AI Search API via the `LlmRequest`. This lack of visibility can hinder troubleshooting efforts related to tool configuration.

**Solution:**
This PR enhances the `VertexAiSearchTool` by adding a **debug-level log statement** within the `process_llm_request` method. This log precisely records the parameters being used for the Vertex AI Search configuration just before it's appended to the `LlmRequest`.

This provides developers with crucial visibility into the tool's runtime behavior when debug logging is enabled, significantly improving the **debuggability** of agents using this tool. Corresponding unit tests were updated to rigorously verify this new logging output using `caplog`. Additionally, minor fixes were made to the tests to resolve Pydantic validation errors.

Co-authored-by: Xuan Yang <xygoogle@google.com>

- feat!: Migrate DatabaseSessionService to use JSON serialization schema

Also provide a command line tool `adk migrate session` for DB migration

Addresses https://github.com/google/adk-python/discussions/3605
Addresses https://github.com/google/adk-python/issues/3681

To verify:
```
# Start one postgres DB
docker run --name my-postgres -d -e POSTGRES_DB=agent  -e POSTGRES_USER=agent  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=agent  -e PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata -v pgvolume:/var/lib/postgresql/data -p 5532:5432 postgres

# Connect to an old version of ADK and produce some query data
adk web --session_service_uri=postgresql://agent:agent@localhost:5532/agent

# Check out to the latest branch and restart ADK web
# You should see error log ask you to migrate the DB

# Start a new DB
docker run --name migration-test-db \
  -d \ --rm \ -e POSTGRES_DB=agent \ -e POSTGRES_USER=agent \ -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=agent -e PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata -v migration_test_vol:/var/lib/postgresql/data -p 5533:5432 postgres

# DB Migration
adk migrate session \
  --source_db_url="postgresql://agent:agent@localhost:5532/agent" \
  --dest_db_url="postgresql://agent:agent@localhost:5533/agent"

# Run ADK web with the new DB
adk web --session_service_uri=postgresql+asyncpg://agent:agent@localhost:5533/agent

# You should see the data from old DB is migrated
```

- fix: Optimize Stale Agent with GraphQL and Search API to resolve 429 Quota errors

Merge https://github.com/google/adk-python/pull/3700

### Description
This PR refactors the `adk_stale_agent` to address `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` errors encountered during workflow execution. The previous implementation was inefficient in fetching issue history (using pagination over the REST API) and lacked server-side filtering, causing excessive API calls and huge token consumption that breached Gemini API quotas.

The new implementation switches to a **GraphQL-first approach**, implements server-side filtering via the Search API, adds robust concurrency controls, and significantly improves code maintainability through modular refactoring.

### Root Cause of Failure
The previous workflow failed with the following error due to passing too much context to the LLM and processing too many irrelevant issues:
```text
google.genai.errors.ClientError: 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.
Quota exceeded for metric: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_paid_tier_input_token_count
```
### Key Changes

#### 1. Optimization: REST → GraphQL (`agent.py`)
*   **Old:** Fetched issue comments and timeline events using multiple paginated REST API calls (`/timeline`).
*   **New:** Implemented `get_issue_state` using a single **GraphQL** query. This fetches comments, `userContentEdits`, and specific timeline events (Labels, Renames) in one network request.
*   **Refactoring:** The complex analysis logic has been decomposed into focused helper functions (_fetch_graphql_data, _build_history_timeline, _replay_history_to_find_state) for better readability and testing.
*   **Configurable:** Added GRAPHQL_COMMENT_LIMIT and GRAPHQL_TIMELINE_LIMIT settings to tune context depth
*   **Impact:** Drastically reduces the data payload size and eliminates multiple API round-trips, significantly lowering the token count sent to the LLM.

#### 2. Optimization: Server-Side Filtering (`utils.py`)
*   **Old:** Fetched *all* open issues via REST and filtered them in Python memory.
*   **New:** Uses the GitHub Search API (`get_old_open_issue_numbers`) with `created:<DATE` syntax.
*   **Impact:** Only fetches issue numbers that actually meet the age threshold, preventing the agent from wasting cycles and tokens on brand-new issues.

#### 3. Concurrency & Rate Limiting (`main.py` & `settings.py`)
*   **Old:** Sequential execution loop.
*   **New:** Implemented `asyncio.gather` with a configurable `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT` (set to 3).
*   **New:** Added `urllib3` retry strategies (exponential backoff) in `utils.py` to handle GitHub API rate limits (HTTP 429) gracefully.

#### 4. Logic Improvements ("Ghost Edits")
*   **New Feature:** The agent now detects "Ghost Edits" (where an author updates the issue description without posting a new comment).
*   **Action:** If a silent edit is detected on a stale candidate, the agent now alerts maintainers instead of marking it stale, preventing false positives.

### File Comparison Summary

| File | Change |
| :--- | :--- |
| `main.py` | Switched from `InMemoryRunner` loop to `asyncio` chunked processing. Added execution timing and API usage logging. |
| `agent.py` | Replaced REST logic with GraphQL query. Added logic to handle silent body edits. Decomposed giant get_issue_state into helper functions with docstrings. Added _format_days helper. |
| `utils.py` | Added `HTTPAdapter` with Retries. Added `get_old_open_issue_numbers` using Search API. |
| `settings.py` | Removed `ISSUES_PER_RUN`; added configuration for CONCURRENCY_LIMIT, SLEEP_BETWEEN_CHUNKS, and GraphQL limits. |
| `PROMPT_INSTRUCTIONS.txt` | Simplified decision tree; removed date calculation responsibility from LLM. |

### Verification
The new logic minimizes token usage by offloading date calculations to Python and strictly limiting the context passed to the LLM to semantic intent analysis (e.g., "Is this a question?").

*   **Metric Check:** The workflow now tracks API calls per issue to ensure we stay within limits.
*   **Safety:** Silent edits by users now correctly reset the "Stale" timer.
*   **Maintainability:** All complex logic is now isolated in typed helper functions with comprehensive docstrings.

Co-authored-by: Xuan Yang <xygoogle@google.com>

- feat(bigquery): Add labels support to BigQueryToolConfig for job tracking and monitoring

Merge https://github.com/google/adk-python/pull/3583

**Please ensure you have read the [contribution guide](https://github.com/google/adk-python/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before creating a pull request.**

### Link to Issue or Description of Change

**1. Link to an existing issue (if applicable):**

- Closes: #3582

**2. Or, if no issue exists, describe the change:**

_If applicable, please follow the issue templates to provide as much detail as
possible._

**Problem:**
Currently, the BigQuery tool in ADK does not provide a way for developers to add custom labels to BigQuery jobs created by their agents. This makes it difficult to:

Track and monitor BigQuery costs associated with specific agents or use cases
Organize and filter BigQuery jobs in the Google Cloud Console
Implement billing attribution and resource organization strategies
Differentiate between jobs from different environments (dev, staging, production)
While the tool automatically adds an internal adk-bigquery-tool label with the caller_id, there's no mechanism for users to add their own custom labels for tracking and monitoring purposes.

**Solution:**
Add a labels configuration field to BigQueryToolConfig that allows users to specify custom key-value pairs to be applied to all BigQuery jobs executed by the agent. The solution should:

Configuration Option: Add an optional labels parameter to BigQueryToolConfig accepting a dictionary of string key-value pairs
Validation: Ensure labels follow BigQuery's requirements (non-empty string keys, string values)
Job Application: Automatically apply configured labels to all BigQuery jobs alongside the existing internal labels Documentation: Provide clear documentation on how to use labels for tracking and monitoring

- docs(adk): fix run_async example and correct ticketId payload key

Merge https://github.com/google/adk-python/pull/3875

# Problem
The example in `contributing/samples/human_in_loop/README.md` shows:

```python
await runner.run_async(...)
```

However, `run_async` returns an **async generator**, so awaiting it raises:

```
TypeError: object async_generator can't be used in 'await' expression
```

Additionally, the example payload uses `"ticket-id"` while ADK tools and other examples use `"ticketId"`, creating a mismatch that breaks copy/paste usage.

# Solution
- Updated the snippet to consume the async generator correctly:

```python
async for event in runner.run_async(...):
    ...
```

- Aligned the payload key from `"ticket-id"` → `"ticketId"` for consistency with ADK schema and other examples.

These changes make the example runnable and consistent with the API’s actual behavior.

# Testing Plan
This PR is a **small documentation correction**, so no unit tests are required per contribution guidelines.

- Verified the corrected snippet manually to ensure it no longer raises `TypeError`.

- fix: Redirect LiteLLM logs from stderr to stdout

LiteLLM's StreamHandlers output to stderr by default. In cloud environments like GCP, stderr output is treated as ERROR severity regardless of actual log level, causing INFO-level logs to be incorrectly classified as errors.

This change redirects LiteLLM loggers to stdout in two places:
- In `lite_llm.py`: Immediately after litellm import
- In `logs.py`: When `setup_adk_logger()` is called (with guard to check if litellm is imported)

- fix: Normalize multipart content for LiteLLM's ollama_chat provider

LiteLLM's `ollama_chat` provider does not accept array-based content in messages. This change flattens multipart content by joining text parts or JSON-serializing non-text parts before sending the request to the LiteLLM completion API. This ensures compatibility with Ollama's chat endpoint.

Дополнительно, адаптер MCP Apps был обновлен для соответствия последней спецификации и типу MIME.
updates.source_content:
- chore: update dependencies

- chore: Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct

This document outlines the Code of Conduct for community members, detailing our pledge, standards of behavior, enforcement responsibilities, and consequences for violations.

- fix(client): use type-only imports for @modelcontextprotocol/sdk types (#157)

Change value imports to `import type` syntax for SDK types to prevent
bundlers from including Node.js server code in browser builds.

When bundling @mcp-ui/client for pure browser environments, the
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk's server-side code (which imports Express)
was being included due to the import chain, causing "require is not
defined" errors at runtime.

Since the SDK is only used for TypeScript types (not runtime values),
using `import type` ensures these imports are stripped at compile time
and don't trigger bundling of the SDK's server-side modules.

Files changed:
- UIResourceRendererWC.tsx: EmbeddedResource type
- metadataUtils.ts: Resource type
- processResource.ts: EmbeddedResource, Resource types
- UIResourceRenderer.unmocked.test.tsx: EmbeddedResource type

updates.source_content:
- `StreamlitMarkdown` - module level plugin cache (#13152)

React's `StrictMode` exposed some opportunities to improve the recently added lazy loading for `StreamlitMarkdown`'s plugins:`rehype-katex`,`rehype-raw`, & `remark-emoji`

Component is now StrictMode compatible, with improved performance (plugins load once per app, not per component instance), and better handle plugin load failure (render as plain text).

This PR better makes the following changes:
* **Module-level caching**: Moved plugin storage outside React's
component lifecycle to share across instances and persist across
re-renders
* **Adds custom `useLazyPlugin` hook**: Consolidated three
nearly-identical useEffect blocks into a single reusable hook with
proper cleanup handling
* **Extraction to `utils.ts`**: Moved all plugin-related logic (types,
loaders, cache, helpers, hook) to a dedicated file

updates.title: Updates in develop (9 commits)
updates.summary_ru: Это обновление вносит значительные улучшения в возможности рендеринга Streamlit, в частности, добавляя поддержку форматирования Markdown для параметров `value` и `delta` компонента `st.metric`. Была реализована новая важная внутренняя функция `TransientNode` во многих посетителях, чтобы улучшить обработку и рендеринг динамических или временных элементов во время обновлений приложения. Дополнительно, обновление включает рефакторинг для повышения согласованности, удаление неиспользуемого кода и оптимизацию рабочих процессов CI/CD.
updates.source_content: - Support for markdown in the metrics value and delta parameters (#13094) ## Describe your changes I have added markdown rendering components to value and delta It is functional like in the screenshot but I do not know how to deal with conflicting chars like - or $ I see 3 options: 1. add backslashes \ or back ticks ` to these values, so that they get disabled 2. add a new markdown enabled parameter to st.metric so that the user will have to choose if they want to have markdown behavior or not 3. add it like this with a hint for the user that he should use back ticks or backslashes when adding $ Please let me know what behavior is most desirable. Code in my Screenshot: ``` st.metric( label="Temperature", value="70 °F $ **markdown**", delta=r"-1.2 °F \$ *markdown* $x^2 + y^2 = z^2$", ) ``` ## Screenshot or video (only for visual changes) ## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable) - Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11773 - Related to https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6665 ## Testing Plan - Added unit & e2e tests. --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. --- > [!NOTE] > Render `st.metric` value and delta using Markdown instead of plain text. > > - **Frontend (Metric)**: > - Render metric value and delta with `StreamlitMarkdown` (Markdown enabled, `allowHTML=false`, `inheritFont`). > - Preserve existing spacing by padding `metricValue` with spaces. > - Minor refactor: destructure `element.body` as `metricValue`. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit df8ebfa5f678b8e22e9db5359e52e2d625334ff4. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot). --------- Co-authored-by: Copilot <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com> Co-authored-by: lukasmasuch - Lower flaky-verify workflow to 25 runners (#13160) ## Describe your changes The `flaky-verify` workflow is very useful but also somewhat expensive. It stacked up 17k minutes (of the 8 core job) this month. Lowering this to 25 runners, which verifies that the probability of workflow failure is < 0.16% which should be more than fine for us: This change also adds another step to auto-remove the `flaky-verify` label when run. --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - [chore] Remove unused react-app-env.d.ts file (#13170) ## Describe your changes Removed the `react-app-env.d.ts` file from the frontend library. This file contained a reference to React Scripts types which is no longer needed. ## Testing Plan - No additional tests are needed as this is removing an unused type reference file - The application should build and run normally without this file - Existing tests should pass without modification --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - Migrate spinner to a Mixin (#12829) ## Describe your changes Refactored the `spinner` function to be a mixin class method instead of a standalone function. This change follows the pattern used for other Streamlit elements, making the codebase more consistent. Key changes: - Created a `SpinnerMixin` class in `elements/spinner.py` - Added the mixin to the `DeltaGenerator` class - Updated imports in `__init__.py` to expose the spinner function from `_main` instead of directly from the elements module - Updated references to the spinner function in cache_utils.py and tests ## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable) ## Testing Plan - No additional tests needed as this is a refactoring that preserves existing functionality - All existing spinner tests have been updated to use the new implementation and continue to pass - The functionality remains identical, just the implementation structure has changed --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - [chore] Remove unused baseconsts module and related mock (#13169) ## Describe your changes Removed the unused `baseconsts.ts` file from the frontend library which only contained a `FETCH_PARAMS` constant that wasn't being used anywhere. Also removed the corresponding mock in `App.test.tsx` since it's no longer needed. ## Testing Plan - No additional tests are needed as this is removing unused code - Existing tests should continue to pass, confirming that the removed code wasn't being used --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - Implement visitTransientNode on RenderNodeVisitor (#12825) ## Describe your changes Added support for rendering `TransientNode` elements in the `RenderNodeVisitor` class. This implementation: - Adds a new `visitTransientNode` method that properly renders both transient elements and their anchor - Ensures transient elements get unique keys with a `transient-{n}` format - Maintains proper element collection order in the visitor - Supports both cases where an anchor may or may not be present Updated the `OptionalReactElement` type to `OptionalReactElements` to better handle arrays of elements that can be returned from visitor methods. ## Testing Plan - Added comprehensive unit tests for the new `visitTransientNode` method - Tests cover key generation, element ordering, multiple transient node handling, and different anchor scenarios - Existing tests were updated to accommodate the type changes --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - Implement visitTransientNode on SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor (#12824) ## Describe your changes Implemented the `replaceTransientNodeWithSelf` method on all `AppNode` implementations to properly handle transient node replacement during delta updates. This method allows nodes to decide how to best replace a transient node with themselves, which is crucial for maintaining proper state during incremental updates. Key changes: - Added `replaceTransientNodeWithSelf` to the `AppNode` interface - Implemented the method in `BlockNode`, `ElementNode`, and `TransientNode` classes - Updated `SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor` to use this method when replacing transient nodes - Added comprehensive tests for all implementations ## Testing Plan - Unit Tests: Added extensive test coverage for the new `replaceTransientNodeWithSelf` method in all node types - Tests verify correct behavior for different scenarios: - When script run IDs differ - When transient nodes are empty - When nodes need to be filtered - When timestamps determine which node to keep --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - Implement visitTransientNode on most visitors (#12823) ## Describe your changes We can implement some of the details for Transient Nodes in the visitors. We ignore two places: - **SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor** - This is a bit complicated and it will be separated out. - **RenderNodeVisitor** - This will be adjusted with the new key setup needed for Transient objects to work properly ## Testing Plan - Unit tests for the changes are implemented - All remaining tests must pass --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - Introduce TransientNode (#12822) ## Describe your changes Now we will add some transiency. Transient is special, so we will implement a TransientNode. This change includes adding a method to every visitor and adding an implementation for the DebugVisitor. ## Testing Plan - JS Unit Tests - There's no way this node is introduced yet, so there are no other tests. --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license.

Updates `@vitejs/plugin-react-swc` from 4.1.0 to 4.2.2
Release notes

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react-swc's releases.

plugin-react-swc@4.2.2

Update code to support newer rolldown-vite (#978)

rolldown-vite will remove optimizeDeps.rollupOptions in favor of optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions soon. This plugin now uses optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions to support newer rolldown-vite. Please update rolldown-vite to the latest version if you are using an older version.

plugin-react@4.2.1

Remove generic parameter on Plugin to avoid type error with Rollup 4/Vite 5 and skipLibCheck: false.

I expect very few people to currently use this feature, but if you are extending the React plugin via api object, you can get back the typing of the hook by importing ViteReactPluginApi:

import type { Plugin } from 'vite'
import type { ViteReactPluginApi } from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export const somePlugin: Plugin = {
name: 'some-plugin',
api: {
reactBabel: (babelConfig) => {
babelConfig.plugins.push('some-babel-plugin')
},
} satisfies ViteReactPluginApi,
}

plugin-react-swc@4.2.1

Fix @vitejs/plugin-react-swc/preamble on build (#962)

plugin-react@4.2.0

Update peer dependency range to target Vite 5

There were no breaking change that impacted this plugin, so any combination of React plugins and Vite core version will work.

Align jsx runtime for optimized dependencies

This will only affect people using internal libraries that contains untranspiled JSX. This change aligns the optimizer with the source code and avoid issues when the published source don't have React in the scope.

Reminder: While being partially supported in Vite, publishing TS & JSX outside of internal libraries is highly discouraged.

plugin-react-swc@4.2.0

Add @vitejs/plugin-react-swc/preamble virtual module for SSR HMR (#890)

SSR applications can now initialize HMR runtime by importing @vitejs/plugin-react-swc/preamble at the top of their client entry instead of manually calling transformIndexHtml. This simplifies SSR setup for applications that don't use the transformIndexHtml API.

Use SWC when useAtYourOwnRisk_mutateSwcOptions is provided (#951)

Previously, this plugin did not use SWC if plugins were not provided even if useAtYourOwnRisk_mutateSwcOptions was provided. This is now fixed.

plugin-react@4.1.1

  • Enable retainLines to get correct line numbers for jsxDev (fix #235)

    Mypy no longer supports running with Python 3.9, which has reached end-of-life. When running mypy with Python 3.10+, it is still possible to type check code that needs to support Python 3.9 with the --python-version 3.9 argument. Support for this will be dropped in the first half of 2026!

    Contributed by Marc Mueller (PR 20156).

    Mypy 1.19

    We’ve just uploaded mypy 1.19.0 to the Python Package Index (PyPI). Mypy is a static type checker for Python. This release includes new features, performance improvements and bug fixes. You can install it as follows:

    python3 -m pip install -U mypy

    You can read the full documentation for this release on Read the Docs.

    Python 3.9 Support Ending Soon

    This is the last mypy feature release that supports Python 3.9, which reached end of life in October 2025.

    Performance Improvements

    • Switch to a more dynamic SCC processing logic (Ivan Levkivskyi, PR 20053)
    • Speed up type aliases (Ivan Levkivskyi, PR 19810)

    Fixed‑Format Cache Improvements

    Mypy uses a cache by default to speed up incremental runs by reusing partial results from earlier runs. Mypy 1.18 added a new binary fixed-format cache representation as an experimental feature. The feature is no longer experimental, and we are planning to enable it by default in a future mypy release (possibly 1.20), since it's faster and uses less space than the original, JSON-based cache format. Use --fixed-format-cache to enable the fixed-format cache.

    Mypy now has an extra dependency on the librt PyPI package, as it's needed for cache serialization and deserialization.

    Mypy ships with a tool to convert fixed-format cache files to the old JSON format. Example of how to use this:

    $ python -m mypy.exportjson .mypy_cache/.../my_module.data.ff

updates.summary_ru: Это обновление включает исправления конфликтов отображения навигации и проблем с изменением размера `st.logo` при использовании верхней навигации. Кроме того, выпуск содержит рефакторинг обработки директив Markdown для улучшения организации кода и оптимизации, направленные на сокращение избыточных тематических снимков тестов.
updates.source_content: - [fix] Do not render sidebar nav when top nav enabled (#13227) ## Describe your changes - Fixes a regression where both the Sidebar and Top nav would be visible when navigation is set to `top`. ## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable) Fixes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13224 ## Testing Plan - Adds e2e tests --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - Fix unexpected shrinking of logo with top nav (#13226) ## Describe your changes Fixes an issue with `st.logo` resizing/shrinking to unexpected sizes if top navigation is used. ## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable) - Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13225 ## Testing Plan - Added e2e test. --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license. - Extract unsupported directive cleanup into separate plugin (#13138) ## Summary Refactors markdown directive handling to improve code organization. ## Changes - Extracted unsupported directive cleanup logic from `createRemarkColoringAndSmall()` into dedicated `createRemarkUnsupportedDirectivesCleanup()` function - Plugin now runs last in the pipeline to ensure it only catches directives not handled by other plugins ## Rationale The cleanup logic for unsupported directives is a general fallback mechanism, not specific to color/small directives. component. This change:
